BiblicalUsage: Çâgad is the word for prostrating oneself in homage, and in Isaiah it is the word for what men do before their idols. The prophet shows them bowing down to the work of their own hands, falling before a god of wood that cannot answer. It appears 4 times, all in Isaiah, and every one of them is about false worship.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God will not share His glory with a carved image. Çâgad shows why: the bow that belongs to Him alone is given to wood and stone.
